text:
[Doc: POL-ACAD-EX-01 | Version: v4.0 (2025 Mandatory Senate Revision) (2025) | Section: SECTION 1: REGULATORY PURPOSE, SCOPE, AND STATUTORY DEFINITI | Clause: Clause 1.1 | Page: 1]
Clause 1.1 (Purpose and Institutional Scope): This policy establishes the binding regulatory framework governing
undergraduate and postgraduate taught students who are prevented from attending scheduled end-of-semester written
examinations, laboratory practical examinations, Objective Structured Clinical/Practical Examinations (OSCE/OSPE), or
formal viva voce assessments due to acute, unforeseen medical circumstances. All faculties, examination boards, and
administrative registries must enforce the timelines and evidentiary standards specified herein.

section_title: SECTION 2: THE 'FIT-TO-SIT' DOCTRINE AND MID-EXAMINATION INCAPACITATION
text:
[Doc: POL-ACAD-EX-01 | Version: v4.0 (2025 Mandatory Senate Revision) (2025) | Section: SECTION 2: THE 'FIT-TO-SIT' DOCTRINE AND MID-EXAMINATION INC | Clause: Clause 2.1 | Page: 2]
Clause 2.1 (Strict Enforcement of the Fit-to-Sit Declaration): The University operates a strict 'Fit-to-Sit' regulatory
regime. By entering an examination room, receiving the question paper, and signing the attendance register, a student
formally declares that they are medically and psychologically fit to undertake the examination. Retrospective medical
claims submitted after a student has completed an examination—or after provisional marks have been published—shall be
summarily rejected by theExaminations Committee.

sitting is legally binding and cannot be annulled by a medical certificate obtained later that day.

text:
[Doc: POL-ACAD-EX-01 | Version: v4.0 (2025 Mandatory Senate Revision) (2025) | Section: SECTION 4: VALID VS. INVALID GROUNDS FOR EXAMINATION CONSIDE | Clause: Clause 4.1 | Page: 3]
Clause 4.1 (Admissible Medical Evidence): To qualify for an uncapped deferred examination (`I-Med`), medical
evidence must demonstrate an acute, incapacitating medical condition assessed contemporaneously by an
SLMC-registered medical practitioner or government hospital specialist (see POL-MED-WF-04 Section 2). For inpatient
hospitalizations (such as a 10-day admission for dengue hemorrhagic fever, appendectomy, pneumonia, or acute trauma),
the student must provide both the Official Inpatient Admission & Discharge Ticket and the Ward Consultant's Clinical
Summary covering all missed examination dates.

Clause 5.1 (Administration of Deferred Examinations): Students granted an `I-Med` grade shall sit the deferred
examination during the official Supplementary & Deferred Examination Window, normally scheduled four (4) to six (6)
weeks after the publication of main semester results. An approved `I-Med` sitting is treated as a First-Sit attempt: the
student is eligible for the full mark range (0%–100%), no deferred examination fee is charged, and the transcript reflects a
normal first-attempt grade once completed.

Clause 5.2 (Medical Absence from a Scheduled Deferred Examination): The University does not organize individual
ad-hoc third examination sittings within the same semester. If a student granted an `I-Med` deferral is medically
incapacitated a second time during the Supplementary Examination Window, the student must submit a fresh `Form
EC-01` within 5 working days. Upon verification, the student's `I-Med` status is carried forward to the next regular semester
offering of the module, or—if total pending credits exceed 30 credits—the student is placed on Temporary Medical
Intercalation under `HBK-ACAD-PR-05` Section 3.3.

Clause 5.4 (Examination Medical Appeals Procedure): A student whose `Form EC-01` application is rejected by the
Faculty EC Panel may lodge a formal appeal to the Senate Examinations Appeals Board using Form APP-EX-02 within
ten (10) working days of receiving the rejection notice. An appeal is admissible only on two grounds: (a) availability of
new hospital or diagnostic evidence that could not reasonably have been obtained within the original 5-working-day
window, or (b) demonstrable procedural irregularity in the processing of the original application.

Clause 1.1 (Mandatory 80% Baseline Attendance Threshold): Regular participation in scheduled academic activities is
a foundational requirement for degree accreditation. Every full-time undergraduate and postgraduate student must
maintain a minimum cumulative attendance of eighty percent (80%) in each registered module across all scheduled
lectures, tutorials, workshops, and practical sessions during a fifteen-week teaching semester to be eligible to sit the Final
Examination.

text:
[Doc: POL-ACAD-AT-02 | Version: v3.2 (2025 Mandatory Senate Revision) (2025) | Section: SECTION 1: STATUTORY ATTENDANCE REQUIREMENT AND RECORDING ME | Clause: Clause 1.2 | Page: 1]
Clause 1.2 (Supersession of 2023 Attendance Floor): Effective 01 January 2025, this policy (POL-ACAD-AT-02 v3.2)
supersedes Clause 5.2 of the 2023 Student Handbook (`HBK-ACAD-PR-05` v1.8). Whereas the 2023 Handbook permitted
medical attendance condonation down to 60%, the 2025 Senate Revision establishes a standard medical condonation
zone of 70%–79% and an absolute hard floor of 65% ( strictly restricted to inpatient hospitalization under Clause 3.1). Any
student falling below 65% attendance is automatically barred from final examinations (`NQ / Barred`).
ATTENDANCE GOVERNANCE DEFINITIONS (PART A)
• Standard Eligibility (80%–100%): Automatic clearance to
download the Final Examination Admission Card without
administrative intervention.
• Medical Condonation Zone (70%–79%): Attendance deficit
excusable by the Head of Department upon submission of
Form ATT-02A and CMO-verified medical certificates.
• Hospitalization Waiver Zone (65%–69%): Exceptional
condonation requiring Dean's approval, Inpatient Hospital
Discharge Summary (>= 7 days), and Form ATT-02B.
ATTENDANCE GOVERNANCE DEFINITIONS (PART B)
• Mandatory De-Registration (< 65%): Absolute regulatory
floor. Students below 65% cannot sit final exams regardless of
reason and must apply for Semester Intercalation.
• Form ATT-02A: Standard Medical Absence & Attendance
Condonation Request Form (submitted within 5 working days
of return to classes).
• Form ATT-02B: Extended Hospitalization Academic
Catch-Up & Dean's Attendance Waiver Agreement.

Clause 2.1 (Important Principle — Medical Certificates Do Not Convert 'Absent' Marks to 'Present'): Students must
understand that submitting a medical certificate does not artificially inflate raw biometric attendance percentages in the
Learning Management System (LMS). Instead, verified medical certificates authorize the Registry to reclassify unexcused
absences as Medically Justified Absences (MJA), enabling the student to qualify for formal Attendance Condonation
when their raw attendance falls below the 80% statutory threshold.

section_title: SECTION 1: GOVERNANCE OF CONTINUOUS ASSESSMENT AND DEADLINE INTEGRITY
text:
[Doc: POL-ACAD-CW-03 | Version: v3.0 (2025 Mandatory Senate Revision) (2025) | Section: SECTION 1: GOVERNANCE OF CONTINUOUS ASSESSMENT AND DEADLINE  | Clause: Clause 1.2 | Page: 1]
Clause 1.2 (Supersession of Legacy 2023 Extension and Penalty Rules): Effective 01 January 2025, this policy
(POL-ACAD-CW-03 v3.0) explicitly supersedes Clauses 5.3 and 5.4 of the 2023 Student Handbook (`HBK-ACAD-PR-05`
v1.8). Specifically: (a) the legacy rule permitting individual lecturers to grant 21-day extensions is revoked and replaced by
the Three-Tier Extension Framework (maximum 14 calendar days) in Section 2; and (b) the legacy late penalty of 2%
per day up to 10 days is revoked and replaced by a strict deduction of five percent (5%) per working day up to 5
working days in Section 4.
COURSEWORK EXTENSION DEFINITIONS (PART A)
• Tier 1 Extension (1–3 Working Days): Short-term extension
approved by the Module Leader via Form EXT-03A for acute
minor illness or outpatient consultation.
• Tier 2 Extension (4–7 Working Days): Standard medical
extension approved by the Head of Department via Form
EXT-03B with CMO-verified SLMC certificate.
• Tier 3 Extension (8–14 Calendar Days): Maximum
extension for inpatient hospitalization (e.g., 10-day admission)
approved by Faculty EC Panel via Form EXT-03C.
COURSEWORK EXTENSION DEFINITIONS (PART B)
• Deferred Coursework ('I-Med-CW'): Granted when
hospitalization exceeds 14 days, deferring submission to the
inter-semester Supplementary Assessment Window.
• Retrospective Hospitalization Rule: Allows hospitalized
students unable to apply before a deadline to file Form
EXT-03C within 3 working days after hospital discharge.
• Late Penalty Cut-Off (Day 5): Any unextended submission
more than 5 working days late receives an automatic mark of
0% (Fail).

student's academic registration for one or two semesters without academic penalty. Tuition fees already paid for the
interrupted semester are credited 100% forward to the resumption semester. Prior to returning to campus, the student
must submit a Fit-to-Return Medical Clearance Certificate (Form MED-RTN-06) endorsed by the University CMO at least
fourteen (14) calendar days before the start of the resumption semester.
